items.title: 52300_Trummy Young oral history interview
items.q: the guy I was more close to in that band was Ray Nance

ctx.x: And, of course, let me see. There was a bass player in there, Quinn Wilson. He did -- he was a good arranger. We call him Cupie. And he did quite a bit of writing for Earl back in those days. And he played a string bass and he also played a tuba. And he was a wonderful soloist on tuba, and Earl featured him quite a bit.

So, I don't know, that was a fast resume of the guys in the band with Earl. And, of course, as I mentioned previously that the guy I was more close to in that band was Ray Nance. And the reason I remember him so well was Ray was a fine musician and he had his own little group before he came with Earl. He had a fine little group and they were all youngsters playing around Chicago. And Ray always was a fine violinist. I think he played violin before he did trumpet.

But he admired Louis tremendously and, in fact, all of us did in those days. And so, he played trumpet on the style of Louis, and he sang a lot of Louis' things that Louis did. And he did a heck of a job because he could dance also, you know.
